newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish BGZ gross profit rises to 317 mln PLN in 1H.
newsitem.headline: Polish BGZ gross profit rises to 317 mln PLN in 1H.

text.p: Poland's Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA's (BGZ) pre-tax profit in the first half of 1997 rose to 317.3 million zlotys, 35.1 percent up on the same period last year, the bank said in a statement on Thursday.

It said the bank's balance sheet total was 14.1 billion zlotys at the first half's end versus 11.6 billion zlotys a year earlier and its capital halved to 800 million zlotys from 1.6 billion zlotys a year ago.
BGZ's spokeswoman told Reuters that a decrease in the company's capital stemmed from the bank's need to compensate last year's losses and the expenditure on training centres and the bank's brokerage.

BGZ said first half 1997 revenues on banking activities rose to 419.6 million zlotys from 219.9 million in the first half 1996 with interest revenue at 314.7 million, 89.2 percent higher than in the first half of 1996.
The state treasury holds 66 percent of BGZ shares and the rest belong to 1,200 cooperative banks.

The government plans to amend the current law on cooperative banks to allow the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to buy 14 percent of the bank. Now only cooperative banks may buy BGZ shares from the state treasury.
